newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - March 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - March 24.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- At least 114 policemen and soldiers on active duty are involved in the recent rash of kidnapping nationwide, a report by the Presidental Task Force on Intelligence and Counter Intelligence says. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- More than two million new voters and transferees will troop to 110,000 registration centres in preparation for the May 12 elections (MANILA BULLETIN)
- A breakaway communist faction vows to bring warfare back to the cities with bombing, sniping and guerrilla tactics in an effort to establish a Marxist state in the Philippines. (MANILA STANDARD)
- A JP Morgan analyst says the reelection of President Fidel Ramos will boost the country's image among international investors (MANILA TIMES)

- The Board of Investments is not keen on the proposal to remove textile and cement from the list of economic activities eligible for incentives, trade undersecretary Melito Salazar says. (BUSINESSWORLD)

- The Securities and Exchange Commission has formed a committee which will coordinate with the compliance and surveillance department of the Philippine Stock Exchange in monitoring price manipulation and possible insiders' trading. (BUSINESS DAILY)
- The Department of Finance has warned that the Subic Freeport might become a tax haven by Filipino firms when it becomes an offshore financial centre. (TODAY)
